key_insight: CoReMem treats memory as an investment: coding agents should preserve and use repository knowledge when its expected future benefit justifies the effort of writing and reading it.
problem_solved: Coding agents working through successive tasks must decide what to remember before the next task is known, while adapting to repository changes and avoiding memory that costs more effort than it saves.
method: Introduce Coding-Repository Memory (CoReMem), a framework for memory across successive tasks on an evolving codebase.
Use prospective valuation to balance memory’s expected usefulness against writing and reading costs.
Guide memory design and actor adaptation, including when to act on available memory as a task unfolds.
impact: The framework offers practitioners a way to reason about useful memory rather than simply accumulating more context. The supplied abstract is truncated, so implementation details and measured performance gains cannot be confirmed.
visual_elements: Task timeline showing repository edits and memory passed between successive coding tasks.
Balance scale comparing expected future effort saved with memory writing and reading costs.
Decision flowchart: available memory → assess relevance and cost → use or skip.
Feedback loop connecting memory design, agent behavior, and observed effort.
paper_title: CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation
paper_authors: Peiwen Li, Harshit Verma, Sophia Zhou, Haiwen Wang, Ngoc Bui
